findings.message: This is still a partial fix, not a fix for the whole class. WRITES is a hand-written list of verb forms, and it leaves out the -ing forms and other common ways of saying hours get written. `\b(log|logs|logged|...)\b` does not match 'logging', 'adding', 'booking', 'recording', 'filling' or 'tracking'. Verbs like 'enter', 'enters', 'entered', 'writes', 'updates' and 'puts' aren't in the list at all. A sentence using any of them can claim hours are written with no accept step, and the guard passes it. Fix: match verb stems (`log\w*|add\w*|book\w*|record\w*|fill\w*|track\w*|enter\w*|writ\w*|updat\w*|lands?|goes from`). Add an -ing case and an 'enter' case to the rejected table.
findings.scenario: claims("Agents are logging your hours over MCP.") returns [] because 'logging' fails WRITES, so the guard passes a sentence that says hours are logged without anyone accepting them. claims("Agents enter 2.5 h on your timesheet.") also returns [].
